method: All 101 raw four-byte 0x258 hits were checked against Ghidra disassembly. For 9 hits without a containing Ghidra function, local PE bytes decode to member-adjusting jump thunks; their jump targets were independently decompiled in Ghidra.
thunk_detail: Eight thunks load the address of a +0x258 string/vector-like subobject and one loads a pointer at +0x258, then tail-jump to RVA 0x11f90 or 0x162580. Both targets decompile to standard owned-buffer cleanup, not CSMSFrame bit18 consumers.
coverage: Direct 32-bit displacement byte pattern in executable sections only. Nonbyte/wide operands are not by themselves evidence of CSMSFrame access; packed copies, indirect accesses and other binaries remain outside scope.
conclusion: Among all 101 candidate byte sequences, only the 11 previously known generic CSMSFrame helper accesses directly target the saved outer bit18 byte or its file buffer. No additional byte-sized direct consumer was found; this does not identify the saved field or prove global non-use.
